calibration.basis: Clear labels and legibility support the task, while the familiar layout limits distinctiveness and misplaced focus makes error recovery harder.

primary_action.expected: Focus Past SLA, sort lowest first, then restore highest first.
primary_action.observed: Focus was visible. Rows changed to Central, West, East and then East, West, Central. The highlighted column, arrow and Highest first label showed the active sort.

A-1440.edge_observation: A further Enter reversed the rows to Central, West, East and changed the label to Lowest first.
A-1440.fact_check: East retained 14 open, West 11 and Central 6 through both directions.
A-1440.strength: The highlighted SLA column and East queue callout make the priority easy to scan.
A-1440.weakness: The large desktop table leaves substantial empty space and the treatment is fairly familiar.
A-1440.repair: Tighten the table width or use the space for relevant queue context.

primary_action.expected: Focus Past SLA, sort lowest first, then restore highest first.
primary_action.observed: The focused control remained visible and the rows reversed and returned to East, West, Central. The arrow and Highest first label were visible.

A-390.edge_observation: Another Enter restored Central, West, East with Lowest first visible. The control and all row values fit in the viewport.
A-390.fact_check: East 14, West 11 and Central 6 remained paired with their queues. The rendered table fits at 390 CSS pixels; review metadata reports a 390-pixel layout width.
A-390.strength: The compact table preserves readable labels, values and a clear focus ring.
A-390.weakness: The sort control looks like a highlighted column heading before focus, so its interactivity could be clearer.
A-390.repair: Add a persistent affordance that makes the sort action discoverable without weakening the direction label.

primary_action.expected: Focus Past SLA, sort lowest first, then restore highest first.
primary_action.observed: Focus was visible. Rows changed to Central, West, East and returned to East, West, Central. The colored active column, arrow and Highest first label remained visible.

B-1440.edge_observation: A further Enter changed the order to Central, West, East and displayed Lowest first.
B-1440.fact_check: East retained 14 open, West 11 and Central 6. The displayed total of 5 past SLA agrees with 3 + 2 + 0.
B-1440.strength: The prominent total and expressive typography give the summary a distinctive hierarchy.
B-1440.weakness: The large total does not identify which queue needs attention until the table is read.
B-1440.repair: Pair the total with a concise indication of the highest-risk queue.

primary_action.expected: Focus Past SLA, sort lowest first, then restore highest first.
primary_action.observed: The focused sort control was outlined, the rows reversed and then returned to East, West, Central, and Highest first was visible.

B-390.edge_observation: Another Enter produced Central, West, East with Lowest first visible. The sort control and all rows fit in the viewport.
B-390.fact_check: East 14, West 11 and Central 6 remained paired with their queues. The rendered table fits at 390 CSS pixels; review metadata reports a 390-pixel layout width.
B-390.strength: The summary and table retain their hierarchy and legibility on the narrow screen.
B-390.weakness: The large total consumes vertical space while leaving the specific priority queue implicit.
B-390.repair: Add the highest-risk queue to the total area in compact supporting copy.

preference.reason: Both designs completed the keyboard task and retained correct values at both widths. B has a more distinctive typographic and color treatment while keeping the active sort and focus clear. A is stronger at identifying East as the immediate priority.

unsupported_claims: No claim is made about unseen queue data, screen-reader announcements in an actual screen reader, or horizontal scrolling outside the rendered viewport and reported layout width.
decision: Keep the stock router. The guarded draft improved priority identification, but lost the independent live comparison at both widths.
scope: One frozen dashboard brief with exact unhinted direct responses for both arms. The retry required a real sort reversal and restoration before the scored after capture.
